chunk_findings.detail: The regression is gated on a machine-dependent wall-clock threshold (`elapsed < _BOUND_S`, with `_BOUND_S = 10.0`) around `P.pairs_from(st, Config.load(), ...)`. On a slower CI container, loaded runner, cold filesystem cache, or a `Config.load()` path that does disk/network I/O, the fixed implementation can exceed 10s and fail even though it is scoring only pairs containing the item. Conversely, on a faster CPU the old O(n²) behavior calibrated at “~28s on this machine” can finish under 10s, so this test can pass on the unfixed code. A test for “score only pairs containing the item” should assert the number of scored/compared pairs deterministically (e.g. via a counting hook) rather than rely on wall-clock time.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_dupes_item_speed.py:test_dupes_item_on_a_3000_record_queue_stays_bounded

chunk_findings.detail: The item-scoped assertions can pass on a useless self-only or empty-row result. With `floor=0.10`, a record compared with itself is maximally similar, so if `pair_records` scores/returns only `("R149", "R149")`, the first test passes: `asked` is non-empty, every scored pair contains `R149`, and `all(... for r in rows)` is true. It is also vacuously true for `rows` if the hook fires but no rows are returned. The 3000-record test at line 92 has the same gap: it passes if `rows` is only `[{"a": "R1499", "b": "R1499"}]`. Thus the regression test would not catch a fix that only self-matches the asked item or drops all real duplicate rows, even though the synthetic queue is built to contain many other records sharing the same title/body prefixes.

chunk_findings.detail: This test makes the regression check depend on wall-clock time and ambient machine/load. It builds 3000 records, calls `Config.load()` and `P.pairs_from(...)`, then asserts the whole operation finishes in under 10 seconds. On a loaded CI runner, slow filesystem, or shared developer machine, the fixed code can exceed that bound and the test can fail even though `dupes <item>` is correctly scoped to the item. Conversely, on a sufficiently fast machine the old all-pairs sweep could finish under 10 seconds, so the timing assertion is not a reliable regression guard. A deterministic check such as counting scored pairs or scoring calls would avoid this environment-dependent flakiness.
